name: Focal Myositis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, imaging, and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Presence of a localized, palpable muscle swelling or mass
Muscle biopsy showing focal inflammatory infiltrates with muscle fiber necrosis and regeneration
MRI demonstrating focal muscle edema and inflammation without diffuse involvement
No evidence of systemic inflammatory myopathy or connective tissue disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of localized muscle swelling with confirmatory muscle biopsy showing focal inflammation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic myositis and neoplastic processes.

laboratory: Mild to moderate elevation of serum creatine kinase
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP)
Negative autoantibodies typical of systemic myositis
imaging: MRI showing focal muscle edema and inflammation
Ultrasound demonstrating localized muscle swelling with hypoechoic areas
other: Muscle biopsy revealing focal inflammatory infiltrates with muscle fiber necrosis and regeneration

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse muscle involvement rather than focal
Absence of inflammatory infiltrates on biopsy

redFlags: Systemic symptoms such as high fever or weight loss
Neurological deficits beyond localized muscle weakness
references: Dalakas MC. Inflammatory muscle diseases. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(18):1734-1747.
Meyer A, et al. Focal myositis: clinical and MRI features. Skeletal Radiol. 2017;46(6):789-796.
